issues.body: The audit still checks literal deploy/ references only in workflow YAML and in _rust_build_inputs(), whose corpus is Rust sources and Cargo manifests/lockfile. A selection-gated Rust workflow can invoke a repository helper, local action, reusable workflow, Make/task target, or other config whose body reads deploy/; the workflow itself contains no deploy/ token and the invoked input is outside _rust_build_inputs(). A deploy-only change can therefore alter the Rust lane while classifying orchestration-only, invalidating the claimed non-interference proof and also allowing CodeQL to skip on merge_group.
issues.fix_hint: Audit transitive repository-side inputs reachable from every selection-gated Rust workflow, with a mutation witness where a workflow invokes a helper whose body reads deploy/. If a sound bounded dependency model is not feasible, remove deploy/ from _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE.
issues.title: Deploy dependency audit still misses helper and action indirection

issues.body: test_deploy_lane_workflows_run_no_cargo still treats absence of the literal lowercase substring `cargo` as proof that deploy-lint.yml and deploy-terraform-lint.yml cannot run Rust work. Either workflow can invoke Rust through a local action, reusable workflow, wrapper script, Make/task target, or differently spelled command without that token. Because edits to these workflow definitions themselves are allowlisted, such a change can skip the Rust matrix despite affecting it.
issues.fix_hint: Replace the substring assertion with a fail-closed structural audit of these workflows and all invoked repository-side actions/helpers, including mutation witnesses for indirect Rust execution. Otherwise remove the two workflow definitions from _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE.
issues.title: Cargo substring check still does not prove deploy workflows are Rust-inert

verdict.summary: Round 4 leaves both round-3 fail-open gaps materially unchanged. The deploy inertness audit still scans workflow YAML only for literal deploy-path tokens and scans only Rust/Cargo build inputs; it does not follow selection-gated workflows into repository helpers, local actions, reusable workflows, Make/task targets, or other invoked inputs that can read deploy/. Separately, the two newly allowlisted deploy workflow definitions are still deemed Rust-inert solely by absence of the lowercase substring `cargo`, which cannot exclude indirect or differently spelled Rust execution. Because deploy/ and those workflow files remain in _ORCHESTRATION_SAFE, either gap can cause Rust-affecting changes to skip the Rust matrix and CodeQL merge-group analysis. The same two major findings remain, so progress is stagnant.
